what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: The value cycle closed this stretch and the first honest number it produced is negative. `tools/run_value_cycle_ab.py` ran the same book through the same world twice, changing only which arm sets the renewal margin, and `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab.json` (08:02Z) reads: the flat-rules control earned GBP 1,145,681 net and ended with 172 accounts; the per-customer arm earned GBP 1,052,125 and ended with 170, having churned three more. Realised delta -GBP 93,555 net (-8.2%) and -GBP 118,252 enterprise value, on 69 renewals it priced. That is the thesis's central claim tested for the first time on what the world actually did rather than on what the company believed, and it lost. A loss is a result and not a defect -- the artefact says so in its own words, and a baseline that could not be lost to would never have been a baseline. What matters is that the losing mechanism is now visible in two places and it is the same mechanism twice. First, the arm's commonest answer was a bound and not a customer: of 66 priced renewals, 20 finished at the ceiling, 16 at the floor, 27 were clamped by the price cap, and the modal margin's 24.2% share of the book is exactly those 16 floor cases. The same arm scored offline over 263 accounts gave 187 distinct margins with a 1.9% mode; met by the live chain it collapses to 36 distinct with a 24.2% mode. Second, the belief it maximises against is inflated roughly fivefold: EP1's coupled gap, re-measured at 08:07Z over 33 counted accounts of 263 available, reads mean belief GBP 473.71 against mean realised GBP 100.20, gap 2.529 -- up from 1.76 on 5 accounts a week ago, and anything above 1 means the per-customer lifetime value carries LESS information than handing every account the population mean. The ledger's own truth-window note says the headline is conservative for an over-estimating belief, so the real inflation is larger than that. Against the thesis, then: the loop exists, the baseline exists, the instrument is honest, and the measured advantage from inference is currently negative. That is a backwards step in substance and a forward step in epistemics on the same day, and the honest sentence is that this company does not beat its own flat rules and now knows by how much and roughly why. On the previous focus, the record is clean: all four items were named, all four were drawn, three are finished. The map split landed at `7f11d9c7d`, `load_atoms()` reads 298 atoms from HEAD, `refile()` exists at `tools/maturity_map_store.py:250` and is called from `tools/merge_atom_status.py:597` with mutation tests in both directions and a null control, and the live invariant is clean. The publish-state fix landed -- the hook chain's own failing node IDs now reach `.publish_gate_state.json`. Publishing is live, figures reached origin 0.3h ago, and the operational signal reads green after being red for five hourly checks. The fourth item, EP13, landed its code and did not move its level, which is the only reason it survives below.

focus.what: Find why the per-customer arm's answers come from a bound and fix the mechanism, then re-run the A/B. The evidence is `decision_shape` in `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab.json`: 66 priced, `endpoint_at_ceiling` 20, `endpoint_at_floor` 16, `clamped_by_the_price_cap` 27, modal margin 24.2% of the book, median chosen margin GBP 100.50/MWh. Read `company/pricing/value_based_renewal.py::decide_margin` together with the chain that consumes it in `company/pricing/renewal_rate_chain.py` and establish which bound binds and in which order -- whether the ceiling and floor are the arm's own support endpoints, or the chain's cap clamp landing on top of an already-chosen margin, or both on different accounts. The candidate mechanism is already documented and now reads LATENT: `company/crm/churn_model.py::MAX_CHURN_PROBABILITY = 0.95` leaves five percent of every account modelled as staying at any price, which makes expected contribution monotone increasing in margin and puts the maximiser on whatever ceiling it is given (`WORKER_FINDING_THE_CHURN_MODELS_CAP_MAKES_THE_PROFIT_MAXIMISING_PRICE_UNBOUNDED_2026-08-25`). Do not clamp the arm to hide it: a tighter bound leaves the belief wrong and moves a known defect behind the wall for the company to rediscover, which is the one thing the epistemic design exists to prevent. Fix the belief, re-run `tools/run_value_cycle_ab.py`, and land the new artefact beside the old one rather than over it.
focus.why: The A/B is the only honest instrument the thesis has, and right now it is scoring a ceiling rather than a decision -- more than half the arm's answers were fixed by a bound, and the single commonest answer it gave was the floor. Until the answers come from the customer, the -GBP 93,555 delta measures the arm's endpoints and not its inference, so neither a win nor a loss from this instrument means what the thesis needs it to mean. The median chosen margin of GBP 100.50/MWh against the regulated EBIT allowance of GBP 3.73-8.54/MWh is the same fact from the other side: a real supplier could not charge that, so an arm producing it is not yet making a commercial decision. Finished when the re-run's `decision_shape` shows the bounds are no longer where the arm's answers come from, the record names which mechanism was putting them there, and the resulting delta is a statement about per-customer prediction.

focus.what: Find and fix the mechanism inflating three-horizon CLV magnitude in `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py`. Start from what `docs/observability/coupled_gap_ledger.json` already holds: mean belief GBP 473.71 against mean realised GBP 100.20 over 33 counted accounts, 27 of the 33 flagged magnitude-inflated, 7 sign disagreements, and one single scalar rescale absorbing four fifths of the headline in-sample (`best_single_scale` 0.204, `gap_after_best_single_scale` 0.806). Do NOT apply that scalar -- the ledger labels it an attribution and never a correction, and applying it would be a constant fitted to the very comparison it is then judged by. Read it as the diagnosis it is: four fifths of the error is one systematic magnitude and not per-account noise, so the thing to look for is a horizon, tenure or retention assumption that scales every account at once. The ledger's `truth_window_bias` note says realised spans the whole lifetime while the belief is taken at the first year-end snapshot, which flatters an over-estimating belief -- so rule that in or out before blaming the estimator, and say which it was. Re-measure into the ledger afterwards.
focus.why: Every per-customer decision in this company maximises against this number, the renewal arm in the item above included, so an estimator saying an account is worth roughly five times what the world paid is the upstream half of the loss the A/B just measured. A gap of 2.529 says the estimate carries less information than the population mean -- the thesis losing to the crudest baseline available on the one quantity every per-customer decision rests on. This is also the first real lead the atom has had: five completed lives a week ago could not tell a scale error from noise, and 33 can. Finished when the ledger's next entry is produced by a changed estimator rather than a changed sample, the record names the assumption that was wrong, and belief and realised means are read from the same book.

what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
